import mir_eval

window = 0.1
matching = mir_eval.util.match_events(ref_events, est_events, window)

ref_indices = set(m[0] for m in matching)
est_indices = set(m[1] for m in matching)

# 1. Check that each event is matched at most once
assert len(ref_indices) == len(matching), "Reference indices in matching are not unique"
assert len(est_indices) == len(matching), "Estimated indices in matching are not unique"

# 2. Check that all matches satisfy the window constraint
for i, j in matching:
    assert abs(ref_events[i] - est_events[j]) <= window, f"Match ({i}, {j}) exceeds window {window}"

# 3. Check that the matching is at least maximal (a necessary condition for maximum matching)
unmatched_refs = set(range(len(ref_events))) - ref_indices
unmatched_ests = set(range(len(est_events))) - est_indices

for i in unmatched_refs:
    for j in unmatched_ests:
        assert abs(ref_events[i] - est_events[j]) > window, "Found an unmatched pair within the window (matching is not maximal)"

print(f"__CHECK__ match_events {len(matching)}")
